Pegasus · Work Centre design review · 5 October 2026

One Dismiss on every row. The day's figures back on the page.

Five ways to lay out the Work Centre, all on the current Pegasus shell and all drawn from the same synthetic office. Each one answers issue 1017 (Dismiss was only visible on New cases) and restores the activity figures that left the page in August: New cases today, Sent to Engineer and Reports sent today and this week, Completed this week and E-mails received today. Open today's page drawn from the same data to compare.

One row end

Every row of every list ends in the same icon-only Dismiss, named for its record, always visible. The open row no longer hides a second one. Dismissing takes the record's rows out of every list at once, with no notice and no undo, exactly as the 2 October rulings say; the mockup also moves focus to the next row.

Activity figures

Seven figures in a Today / This week grid. A half that is not defined is simply not drawn, and a failed read shows the section's unavailable notice and no digits, never 0. A strip switch shows each design with the figures in its own place or in one line under the five counts.

Mockup switches

Icon X or text Dismiss (item B), the figures' placement (item I), one Updated clock or one per section (item J), and "Taken until" or the live "Lease expires" (item K). Every state is also a query string, so a screenshot needs no click.

A

Even ledger

Today’s page, every list the same table.

Keeps the five counts and the three tabs. Needs attention, New cases and AI jobs all become the same kind of table, with the next action visible in the row and one Dismiss at the end of every row. The activity figures sit in a strip under the counts.

Why choose it
The smallest change from the page you have now. Nothing moves; everything that was inconsistent becomes consistent.
Tradeoff
New cases and AI jobs stay one click away behind their tabs.

B

Morning brief

Your own day first; the office one click away.

Office / Mine moves into the header and scopes the whole page. Engineers open on Mine, Administrators on Office. The ledger takes the left two thirds; the right column holds the activity table, what is new since you last looked, and the AI jobs you started.

Why choose it
An Engineer sees only what is theirs the moment the page opens, with the office figures beside it.
Tradeoff
An Administrator switches to Office to see everyone’s work, and the full seven-day New cases list leaves the first screen.

C

Split desk

Recommended

No tabs. The whole office on one screen.

The Needs attention ledger keeps its toolbar, chips and groups on the left. A right-hand rail holds the activity table, New cases and AI jobs as compact rows, each section drawn only when it has something to show.

Why choose it
Everything the office needs is visible at once at 1580 and 1440; nothing is hidden behind a tab.
Tradeoff
The ledger is narrower, so Due and Received share a cell, and a long attention list pushes New cases down the rail.
Explore design C →MineAfter a dismissalNothing to show
D

One list

All office work in one time-ordered ledger.

One toolbar (Office / Mine, Find, a Kind dropdown) and one table. New cases since you last looked lead, then Overdue, Due today and Later, then the AI jobs still in progress. The activity figures share the strip with the five counts.

Why choose it
One place to look and one Dismiss rule; the tabs and the chip row both go.
Tradeoff
An arrival sits in the same list as a task, and paging across three sources is a bigger change behind the page.
Explore design D →MineAfter a dismissalNothing to show
E

Flow lanes

Work by stage, with each stage’s throughput in its head.

Four lanes: Arrived (new cases), Waiting (chases, holds, images, Unidentified, Triage), Review (Review, Unassigned, AI drafts and the AI jobs in progress) and Out (what left the office today and this week). The five counts move into the lane heads.

Why choose it
The shape of the office’s day is visible at a glance, and the figures sit where the work they count happens.
Tradeoff
There is no single due order across the page, the lanes are narrow at 1440, and the count strip you placed in September moves.

Recommended: C · Split desk. It answers "multiple tabs" directly, keeps the Needs attention ledger and its rules intact, and puts the figures beside the work an Administrator scans each morning. A is the smallest change. D is the boldest: one list, one rule. B puts the person first. E shows the office by stage.
Try it: dismiss QDOS26203 and watch it leave both Needs attention and New cases, switch Office and Mine, filter by kind, Find BH17RZV, open a row, assign an Engineer, complete the Query response job, and refresh. Read the notes and the lettered sign-off items. These are offline design artifacts and do not establish how the application behaves.
